([[Summerville, South Carolina]]) | college = [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman]] (2018–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 54 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team1 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team2 = →[[Stockton Kings]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team3 = [[Osceola Magic]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team4 = [[Noblesville Boom]] | years5 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team5 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | years6 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team6 = →Noblesville Boom | highlights = * [[NBA G League]] All-Defensive Team ([[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]) * [[Southern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SoCon Player of the Year]] (2023) * [[SoCon]] Defensive Player of the Year (2022) * 2× First-team All-SoCon (2022, 2023) }} '''Jalen Brooks Slawson''' (born October 22, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Noblesville Boom]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman Paladins]]. ==Early life and high school career== Slawson grew up in [[Summerville, South Carolina]] and attended [[Pinewood Preparatory School]].{{cite web |last=Lee |first=Roger |date=January 17, 2017 |title=Slawson steps into leadership role for Panthers |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/journal-scene/sports/slawson-steps-into-leadership-role-for-panthers/article_98243259-5c3f-5965-b144-1a72ad4ddb81.html |access-date=March 16, 2023 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} He was named the Area Player of the Year after averaging 14.6 points, 10.5 rebounds, 4.1 blocks and 3.5 assists per game as a senior.{{cite web |last=Lee |first=Roger |date=May 9, 2018 |title=PREP SPORTS: Slawson named Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/our-gazette/sports/prep_sports_awards/prep-sports-slawson-named-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/article_6c60b48a-b38f-5ad5-bcac-634d3a58ed08.html |access-date=March 16, 2023 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} Slawson committed to playing college basketball for [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman]].{{cite web |last=Lee |first=Roger |date=November 13, 2017 |title=Pinewood Prep hoopsters sign |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/journal-scene/sports/pinewood-prep-hoopsters-sign/article_a5e72814-c127-53fc-80bf-f6c1cf5ac708.html |access-date=March 16, 2023 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} ==College career== Slawson was a key bench player during his freshman season at Furman and became a starter entering his sophomore year. He averaged 8.7 points as a junior.{{cite web |last=Keeler |first=Scott |date=February 18, 2022 |title=Jalen Slawson's bond with coach Bob Richey key to Furman basketball |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/furman/2022/02/18/jalen-slawsons-summerville-sc-furman-basketball-bob-richey/6829947001/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=March 16, 2023 |work=[[The Greenville News]]}} Slawson was named the [[Southern Conference]] (SoCon) Defensive Player of the Year and first-team All-SoCon after averaging 14.5 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.7 blocks per game during his senior season.{{cite web |last=Keeler |first=Scott |date=October 31, 2022 |title=Furman basketball is the SoCon favorite. Now it must handle the hype |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/furman/2022/10/31/furman-basketball-socon-favorite-must-handle-hype/69595537007/ |access-date=March 16, 2023 |work=[[The Greenville News]]}} Slawson decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]] and return to Furman for a fifth season.{{cite web |last=Long |first=Mark |date=March 16, 2023 |title=Furman found NCAAs thanks to college roommates, best friends |url=https://news.yahoo.com/furman-found-ncaas-thanks-college-183409101.html |access-date=October 30, 2023 |work=[[Yahoo.com]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} He was named the [[Southern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SoCon Player of the Year]] as he helped lead the Paladins to their first NCAA tournament appearance in 43 years.{{cite web |last=Sapakoff |first=Gene |date=March 14, 2023 |title=Sapakoff: Jalen Slawson, the heart of Furman’s NCAA Tournament joy |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college/sapakoff-jalen-slawson-the-heart-of-furmans-ncaa-tournament-joy/article_bfbe93f2-c195-11ed-b5b3-976854f9cbda.html |access-date=March 16, 2023 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]}} Slawson averaged 15.6 points, 7.1 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.5 blocks per game on the season.{{cite web|url=https://fox40.com/sports/basketball/kings/sacramento-kings-nba-draft-colby-jones-jalen-slawson/|title=Here’s who the Sacramento Kings selected in the 2023 NBA Draft|first=Jeremiah|last=Martinez|website=[[Fox40.com]]|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=June 26, 2023|archive-date=June 26, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230626001614/https://fox40.com/sports/basketball/kings/sacramento-kings-nba-draft-colby-jones-jalen-slawson/|url-status=dead}} He scored 19 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in the Paladins' 68–67 upset win over [[2022–23 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the first round of the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/march-madness-furmans-jalen-slawson-couldnt-believe-kihei-clarks-fateful-pass-in-upset-of-virginia-204625908.html|title=March Madness: Furman's Jalen Slawson couldn't believe Kihei Clark's fateful pass in upset of Virginia|first=Jason|last=Owens|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=March 16, 2023|access-date=June 26, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2023–2024)=== Slawson was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]] with the 54th overall pick{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Biderman|title=Sacramento Kings select Furman’s Jalen Slawson late in Round 2 of NBA draft. Who is he?|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/article276680031.html|work=[[The Sacramento Bee]]|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} and on July 2, 2023, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with them.{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Sign Jalen Slawson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-jalen-slawson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2023|access-date=July 2, 2023}} Slawson made 12 appearances for the Kings during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 0.7 points, 0.6 rebounds, and 0.2 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jalen Slawson 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4398207/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Osceola Magic (2024–2025)=== On September 11, 2024, Slawson signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],{{cite tweet|author=Orlando Magic PR|title=PRESS RELEASE: @OrlandoMagic sign free agents Jarrett Culver, Myron Gardner, Jalen Slawson and Tre Scott #MakeItMagic|number=1834029427308589566|user=Magic_PR|date=September 11, 2024|access-date=September 11, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Convert Contract of Mac McClung to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-convert-contract-of-mac-mcclung-to-two-way-contract-20241019|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}} Eight days later, he joined the [[Osceola Magic]].{{cite web|title=Osceola Magic Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/osceola-magic-announce-training-camp-roster/n-6160339|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}} ===Indiana Pacers (2025–present)=== On September 9, 2025, Slawson signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]] on an [[Exhibit 10]] contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/09/09/pacers-sign-jalen-slawson-exhibit-10-contract/86065964007/|title=Pacers sign Jalen Slawson to an Exhibit 10 contract; what it means|publisher=IndyStar|date=September 9, 2025|access-date=October 8, 2025|first=Scott|last=Horner}} He was included on the Pacers' training camp roster, with the expectation of playing for the [[Noblesville Boom]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-jalen-slawson-included-on-indianas-camp-roster/|title=Pacers' Jalen Slawson: Included on Indiana's camp roster|publisher=CBS Sports|author=RotoWire Staff|date=October 1, 2025|access-date=October 8, 2025}} Slawson played in his first game with the Pacers in their preseason opener against the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]], scoring nine points.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/10/07/pacers-vs-timberwolves-stats-box-score/86564784007/|title=Pacers vs. Timberwolves stats: How many points did Pascal Siakam score in NBA preseason?|publisher=USA Today|date=October 7, 2025|access-date=October 8, 2025|last=Horner|first=Scott}} On October 18, Slawson was waived by Indiana.{{cite web |title=Pacers Transactions - Oct. 18, 2025 |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-transactions-oct-18-2025 |website=NBA.com}} On October 27, the Noblesville Boom announced Slawson would be part of the 2025–26 training camp roster. {{Cite tweet |author=Noblesville Boom |user=noblesvilleboom |number=1982839015175864784 |date= 27 October 2025 |title=our training camp roster is locked in 🔒time to get to work 💪 |access-date= 27 October 2025}} On November 4, he played in the Boom's first [[Exhibition game|scrimmage]].{{cite news |last=Tannous |first=Christine |title=Noblesville Boom hold scrimmage ahead of season opener at The Arena at Innovation Mile in Noblesville |url=https://www.indystar.com/picture-gallery/sports/basketball/2025/11/04/noblesville-boom-hold-scrimmage-ahead-of-season-opener-at-the-arena-at-innovation-mile/87096081007/ |access-date=6 November 2025 |work=The Indianapolis Star |date=4 November 2025}} On November 5, the Boom announced Slawson would be on their 2025–26 roster.{{cite tweet|author=Noblesville Boom|title=introducing our 2025-26 roster 😈|number=1986192230315381074|user=noblesvilleboom|date=November 5, 2025|access-date=November 5, 2025}} On February 27, 2026, Slawson signed a two-way contract with the Pacers, following [[Quenton Jackson]]'s promotion to a standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Pacers' Jalen Slawson: Gets two-way deal with Indiana|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-jalen-slawson-gets-two-way-deal-with-indiana/|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} Slawson made 13 appearances (including six starts) for Indiana during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 7.3 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 2.8 assists (all career-highs).{{Cite web|title=Jalen Slawson 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4398207/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On July 22, 2026, Slawson signed another two-way contract with the Pacers.{{cite web |title=Pacers Sign Slawson to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-slawson-to-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date= 22 July 2026}}
